text:
Maya: heads up — noticed a regression in tail latency on the short-chat suite after the AWQ packer change rolled yesterday. p95 went from ~120ms to ~230ms on T4 in our dedicated pool. 😬

Arjun: ugh. did the kernel chooser fall back to the serial unpack path? that's where we see spikes historically. can you paste the perf sample?

Maya: here's a quick flame snippet from `perf` on a repro run (1000 warm, 2000 measured):
```
Samples: 2K of event 'cpu-clock'
Overhead  Command  Shared Object              Symbol
  34.1%  worker   libredwood_runtime.so       awq_pack_and_unpack_serial
  18.5%  worker   libredwood_runtime.so       kv_cache_lookup
  12.3%  worker   libmkl.so                  gemm_int8_kernel
   7.2%  worker   libredwood_runtime.so       chunk_align_and_copy
   5.9%  worker   libc.so.6                   memcpy
```

Maya: full perf profile + pprof link: https://ci.internal/runs/3349/artifacts/pack_trace.pb.gz

Priya: interesting — that `chunk_align_and_copy` hit suggests packing alignment is causing extra memcopies. did the packer switch alignment from 64->128 bytes? we changed that recently for AVX512 paths.

Arjun: we did a conservative alignment bump in the AWQ pipeline to avoid misaligned loads on some kernels. but on T4 that forces extra padding and smaller effective group sizes which hurts throughput for short sequences.

Liam: repro command so others can run locally:
```bash
# run the short-chat microbench with AWQ packer enabled
AWQ_PACKER=1 AWQ_ALIGNMENT=128 RUNTIME_PROFILE=1 ./tools/bench_short_chat --model redwood-awq-3b --batch 1 --seq 64 --iters 3000
```

Maya: quick local numbers after flipping AWQ_ALIGNMENT=64: p50 45ms -> 40ms, p95 230ms -> 140ms. not perfect but much better.

Priya: try toggling `group_size` too. AWQ group_size=32/64/128 affects GEMM layout and pack density. my gut says group_size=64 may be sweet on T4 for weight-only quant.

Arjun: noted. I'll run a sweep tonight across {32,64,128} and two alignment settings. Will also enable the new kernel telemetry (kernel_id in trace) so we can see when kernel chooser picks serial vs vectorized path.

perf-ci-bot: CI run queued: https://ci.internal/runs/3350 (bench-matrix: alignment={64,128}, group_size={32,64,128}, kernel-telemetry=on)

Liam: one more angle — the KV cache behavior: our prefetch window was tuned for larger batch sizes. for small-batch low-latency flows we occasionally do extra small memcpy churn when packing keys. try `KVCACHE_PREFETCH_WINDOW=1` to reduce speculative prefetching. helped a customer earlier.

Maya: good call. I tested `KVCACHE_PREFETCH_WINDOW=0` and saw ~8% lower p95 but small regression on throughput for long sequences (expected). we need a policy keyed off request size.

Arjun: ok, plan: 1) run the alignment+group sweep and upload perf traces, 2) add kernel_id telemetry to traces, 3) prototype runtime knob that flips KVCACHE_PREFETCH_WINDOW when seq_len<128 and batch<=2. I'll own (1) and (3). @Maya can you instrument traces with a tiny marker around pack/unpack so we can slice?

Maya: will add markers and a short repro script to the PR. also I'll annotate the pprof with region markers.

Priya: if the kernel chooser is mis-ranking vectorized kernels vs the safety fallback, we may need to adjust the cost model: we weight numerical error slightly more than measured token throughput atm. for these short-chat cases error tolerance might be higher.

Liam: agreed — add an experiment to relax error penalty for small seqs. can we do a per-route override in the routing policy?

Arjun: yes, routing config supports per-route kernel preference. I'll add a test route config and run A/B.

Maya: created a short tracking thread in the perf board and added links to CI. tagging folks: @Arjun (sweep), @Priya (pack alignment ideas), @Liam (kv prefetch knob), I'll drive the trace instrumentation. :thumbsup:

perf-ci-bot: artifacts posted: https://ci.internal/runs/3350/artifacts/matrix-report.html

Priya: quick note — watch out for election of INT8 GEMM kernels that assume packed contiguous groups; if packer adds padding we may break their fast path and fall back. we should add an assert in kernel selector to log padding ratio when falling back. small change but helps debugging.

Arjun: will add that assert and also a counters metric `pack_padding_ratio` exposed to observability.

Maya: thanks. will follow up with the trace PR and microbench numbers when available. closing the loop in this thread once we have the sweep results. :eyes:
